vulnerabilityAlerts.description: A fix for a known vulnerability opens its PR at once, without the 7-day wait or the weekly schedule.

lockFileMaintenance.description: Each month, the lock files' transitive packages move to the newest their ranges allow, in one PR a person merges.
schedule: before 6am on the first day of the month

customManagers.description: The gitleaks release the Security workflow downloads, checked there against that release's checksums.

packageRules.description: Runtime packages: one weekly PR for minor and patch updates, merged by a person after testing on real hardware. Sensor libraries reach a kernel driver, which the CI cannot test.

Build-only packages (analyzers, test tools) never ship to users: their minor and patch updates merge themselves once the CI gate is green. GitHub's auto-merge squashes the PR as a person would, and `rebaseWhen: conflicted` keeps each push to main from rebasing it and restarting the CI before it ever turns green.
The settings window's page pins its npm packages exactly, beside the lockfile. Renovate takes a range strategy only in a rule that names no update type.
The page's minor and patch updates: one weekly PR, merged by a person after its Playwright tests.
GitHub Actions and the CI's tools in their own PR, merged automatically once the CI gate is green, as the build tools are.
Major updates: one PR each, outside the weekly schedule once the 7-day wait is over, reviewed by a person.
